text:
hello claude. i came across a tool called block bench. downloaded it, watched a quick video, and made a car body model. it worked pretty well! and it made it very clear the tooling that we lack for getting pretty much the same effect. actually, we are not that far off to be honest, and i think we can get the exact same capability in house that will let us turn our current approach of the many faces of a vehicle into one face with 4 wheels. here is the car body i made [Image #1] and here is the car body that we currently have in place as a comparison [Image #2] 
now, technically, we can just import the models from block bench into here. but we already have a lot of the capability established from all the uv mesh stuff we did with player models to begin with, i think a smarter play is to catalog exactly what it was from the block bench app that made this possible that we effectively lack. those being loop cut, edge selection, extrude edge, and then create face after you cut out and extrude in to seal the body. and then block bench also lets you paint the uv mapping and thats pretty much what we do also, we have some room for improvement, but i think with the introduction of better tooling that greatly overtime enables less and less prompting you to design models and more time designing the tools for it

so, take a look at the current modeling tools we have in hmsc-int and lets build up a playbook of what we have and how it looks / behaves / acts and then what we want to bring in, how it looks/acts/behaves and then build a plan to shape it up from there
resolution: Delivered the requested modeling-tools playbook at cart/hmsc-int/editors/MESH_EDITOR_PLAYBOOK.md (uncommitted, working tree). It surveys what we have today (every shape bottoms out at non-indexed triangle soup GeometryData; vehicle is a ~60-box procedural stack; building pieces, player models, props, voxel, carve, heightfield, OBJ/GLB import, and the paint/cutout system each catalogued with how they look/behave/act). It names the real gap: the capability is scattered across three half-editors (face-select+paint in buildings, moulded-unwrap-atlas+sculpt in player models, topology-import in props) plus the user's broader thesis that all seven content types (player/clothing/items/vehicle/buildings/world/props) are SEPARATE modeling techniques. The one thing nothing does is edit topology (vertex/edge select, extrude, create-face, loop cut). Proposes one editable EditMesh foundation (verts + n-gon faces + edge adjacency, optional rig-weights/sculpt/per-face-material layers, constructors from voxel/heightfield/carve/primitive/import) that lowers to the same soup everything renders, plus a 5-phase plan (foundation+round-trip, edit shell, the four ops, UV paint, vehicle as first adopter) and a convergence ledger for migrating each silo. Confirmed import works (Desk.glb round-trips) and documented Blockbench export formats (OBJ works today, .gltf is a small add, FBX skip). No code cut yet — awaiting the user's go on where to begin.
